newsitem.title: USA: Southwest Airlines rated top in quality survey.
newsitem.headline: Southwest Airlines rated top in quality survey.

text.p: Southwest Airlines, for the second year in a row, was rated the top U.S. carrier, according to the annual Airline Quality Ratings put out Monday by two Midwest universities.

American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp, and United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp, repeated their second and third place finishes in the report by the School of Business at Wichita State University and the University of Nebraska at Omaha. Transworld Airlines was rated last of the nine carriers surveyed.
The annual survey ranks carriers based on such factors as average age of fleet, on-time arrivals and departures, number of accidents, mishandled baggage and financial stability.
Following the top three airlines were Delta Airlines, Continental Airlines, Northwest Airlines, USAirways, formerly USAir, America West and TWA.
Co-researcher Dean Headley, associate professor of marketing at Wichita State University, said, "We have three distinct groups in the airline industry this time."
He said, "There's one airline that is clearly the leader, a group of five airlines that are good performers and are very competitive, and three airlines that are performing at a lower level."
